content: Does anyone have proof that the inclusion docs#CliffordAlgebra.ι of a module into a clifford algebra on it is injective in certain cases? The only thing I was able to find in mathlib is docs#CliffordAlgebra.not_forall_algebraMap_injective, a counterexample in characteristic 2, but nothing on whether it holds in other characteristics. It would also be great to have a specific choice of linear one-sided inverse to CliffordAlgebra.ι, but I'm not sure what the cleanest way to construct in Lean would be

but nothing on whether it holds in other characteristics.

I thought we had that result; it follows by using docs#CliffordAlgebra.equivExterior
Ah, I guess "two is invertible" is a little strong, ideally it would just be "two is regular"
Oh, interesting. I think that's enough for what I need, thanks
I remember thinking about the titular question, but I don't remember the conclusion
